problem:
Find the limit ${lim}_{t\to 1}[f(t)\cdot g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =⟨t,\,{t}^{2},\,{e}^{1-t}⟩ \\ g(t) & =⟨2t-{t}^{2},\,2t-1,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Limit of a Product of Vector Functions
examples.problem:
Find $\displaystyle \lim_{t \to 2} \left[\mathbf f(t) \cdot \mathbf g(t)\right]$ given that $\mathbf f(t)$ and $\mathbf g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t\,i+t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k \\ g(t) & =(2-t)\,i+\frac{6}{t}\,j-4\,k\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}f(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 2}\operatorname{ln}⁡t)\,i+({lim}_{t\to 2}t)\,j+({lim}_{t\to 2}{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)\,i+2\,j+{2}^{2}\,k \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,i+2\,j+4\,k, \\ {lim}_{t\to 2}g(t) & =({lim}_{t\to 2}(2-t))\,i+({lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{6}{t})\,j+({lim}_{t\to 2}(-4))\,k \\  & =(2-2)\,i+\frac{6}{2}\,j+(-4)\,k \\  & =0\,i+3\,j-4\,k \\  & =3\,j-4\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}[f(t)\cdot g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to 2}g(t) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,i+2\,j+4\,k)\cdot (3\,j-4\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot 0+2\cdot 3+4\cdot (-4) \\  & =-10\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to \,-1}[3f(t)-2g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}+t \\ {e}^{t+1} \\ \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)}{t}\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) \\ 2 \\ \frac{1-2t}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}({t}^{2}+t) \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}{e}^{t+1} \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+1)}{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}(-1)^{2}+(-1) \\ {e}^{-1+1} \\ \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(-1+1)}{(-1)}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}g(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+1) \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}2 \\ {lim}_{t\to \,-1}\frac{1-2t}{{t}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-1+1) \\ 2 \\ \frac{1-2(-1)}{(-1)^{2}+1})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \,-1}[3f(t)-2g(t)] & =3{lim}_{t\to \,-1}f(t)-2{lim}_{t\to \,-1}g(t) \\  & =3[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
